newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. firm Lucent signs Egyptian telephone deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm Lucent signs Egyptian telephone deal.

text.p: U.S. telecommunications firm Lucent Technologies and the Egyptian government signed a memorandum of understanding on Wednesday to set up 260,000 new telephones lines in Cairo.
Officials declined to reveal the value of the deal. But Lucent President for Product Realisation James Brewington told Reuters: "I can tell you it is worth many millions of dollars."
Egyptian Minister of Transport and Communications Soleiman Metwalli and Brewington signed the deal at the Middle East and North Africa economic conference.
The project is to be executed in the next two years and is part of a five-year plan to add five million lines in the whole of the country.
U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor witnessed the signing of the deal and other agreements with U.S. firms on a wide range of projects.
"These business agreements underscore the tremendous amount of commercial activity in the Middle East region," Kantor told reporters.
"We realise the importance of the Middle East to U.S. trade, as well as the importance of strong commercial ties to assist in preserving the peace process," he added.
Lucent is involved in many projects in the region, including Egypt. "We are in Egypt for many years," Brewington said.
"These agreements are only some of the $20 billion in projects located in the Middle East that U.S. firms are competing for, with the support of the U.S. government," Kantor said.
Earlier in November, Egypt started operating a GSM mobile phone network.
